edges.mechanism: Low soil organic carbon (SOC) reduces the substrate available for soil microbes, shrinking microbial biomass and functional diversity.
edges.quantified_effect: Below 0.5% SOC, microbial biomass typically drops 30-50% relative to soils above 1.5% SOC

edges.mechanism: Diverse soil microbial communities improve plant nutrient uptake and flowering vigor, indirectly supporting pollinator forage availability.
edges.quantified_effect: Healthy microbial soils correlate with 10-20% higher flowering density in adjacent forage plants

edges.mechanism: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen and add root biomass, raising SOC through increased organic matter turnover.
Low and erratic rainfall directly reduces soil moisture and surface water recharge.
edges.quantified_effect: Semi-arid regions show 20-40% lower plant-available water in low-rainfall years

edges.mechanism: Reliable water availability reduces drought stress mortality across trophic levels, from vegetation to fauna dependent on it.
edges.quantified_effect: Species richness drops ~25% in habitats with sustained water deficit

edges.mechanism: Higher species survival maintains functional redundancy in an ecosystem, buffering it against further shocks.
Monoculture cropping simplifies land cover structurally and reduces on-farm plant diversity.
Homogeneous, single-crop land use removes hedgerows, field margins, and microhabitats that connect wildlife corridors.
edges.quantified_effect: Monoculture landscapes show 2-3x higher fragmentation index vs. mixed cropping

edges.mechanism: Fragmented habitat isolates populations, reduces gene flow, and shrinks effective foraging/breeding range.
edges.quantified_effect: Each 10% increase in fragmentation index associates with ~8% species richness decline

edges.mechanism: Genetically uniform crops lack the natural pest-predator buffering that polycultures provide.
edges.quantified_effect: Monoculture fields show 2-4x higher pest outbreak frequency

edges.mechanism: Higher pest vulnerability drives increased pesticide use, which harms non-target insects, soil fauna, and pollinators.
edges.quantified_effect: Areas with high pesticide use show 30-45% lower non-target insect abundance

edges.mechanism: Tree-crop integration restores structural complexity and corridors between fragmented patches.
edges.quantified_effect: Agroforestry buffers reduce local fragmentation index by 15-30% over 5 years

edges.mechanism: Tree root systems and leaf litter add deep and surface organic matter beyond what annual crops alone provide.
edges.quantified_effect: +10-20% SOC over 3-5 years in semi-arid agroforestry trials

edges.mechanism: Cover crop residue reduces evaporation and improves soil structure/infiltration, retaining more moisture.
edges.quantified_effect: 10-15% higher soil moisture retention in cover-cropped plots

edges.mechanism: Moist soils sustain more active and diverse microbial communities than dry, crusted soils.
Forest clearing directly severs habitat corridors and reduces core habitat area.
Chemical runoff and air/soil pollutants impose direct toxicological stress on flora and fauna.
